name: Licensing Synthetic Assets and Likeness
title: Licensing Synthetic Assets and Likeness
answer: Licensing synthetic assets and likeness covers agreements that let one party use a person's identifiable features, such as face, voice, body, gait, or persona, in AI-generated or AI-assisted media. It also covers purely synthetic assets, such as generated characters, voices, and images, when those assets are built from licensed data or designed to resemble a real person. The field sits inside intellectual property and trademark strategy because the same deal may touch copyright in source materials, trademark rights in a brand, and right of publicity in a persona. Practitioners handle film, advertising, games, virtual influencers, voice assistants, and training data deals. The core question is what exactly is being licensed, for what uses, and for how long.

sections.body: Licensing synthetic assets and likeness covers agreements that let one party use a person's identifiable features, such as face, voice, body, gait, or persona, in AI-generated or AI-assisted media. It also covers purely synthetic assets, such as generated characters, voices, and images, when those assets are built from licensed data or designed to resemble a real person. The field sits inside intellectual property and trademark strategy because the same deal may touch copyright in source materials, trademark rights in a brand, and right of publicity in a persona. Practitioners handle film, advertising, games, virtual influencers, voice assistants, and training data deals. The core question is what exactly is being licensed, for what uses, and for how long.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on a mix of state right of publicity statutes, contract law, copyright and trademark principles, union and guild agreements, and platform terms. Consent and release forms, chain-of-title records, and data provenance logs are the operational backbone. Technical infrastructure includes identity verification, voice and face capture, watermarking, and provenance standards such as C2PA content credentials. Model training pipelines and synthetic media tools also matter because they determine whether a licensed likeness can be reproduced, altered, or combined with other data. The site tracks 732 AI tools and 686 glossary terms, which reflects how many moving parts a licensing review can involve.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: A licensing engagement usually starts with rights clearance, which means identifying every person and asset that appears in the synthetic output and confirming who controls those rights. Counsel and business teams then draft or review terms that define permitted uses, media, territory, duration, exclusivity, compensation, approval rights, and restrictions on political, adult, or defamatory content. Technical teams may build consent records, audit trails, and model access controls so that a licensed likeness cannot be used outside the agreed scope. Review often includes checking whether the output is transformative, whether it implies endorsement, and whether it triggers disclosure rules. The process is iterative because a synthetic asset can be retrained, fine-tuned, or recombined in ways the original license did not anticipate.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The main risks are right of publicity claims, false endorsement and trademark confusion, copyright disputes over training data, and breach of contract when a synthetic asset is used beyond its license. Provenance matters because a clean chain of consent and a record of how an asset was generated can support defenses and satisfy disclosure requirements. State law varies widely, and post-mortem publicity rights, minors' protections, and biometric privacy rules add layers of compliance. The site tracks 148 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, and 29 AI case law precedents, which shows that courts are still shaping the boundaries. Insurance, indemnities, and audit rights are common contractual tools, but they do not replace clear scoping and accurate records.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward more granular licensing, with separate grants for voice, face, motion, and persona, and shorter terms tied to specific campaigns or model versions. Expect more state legislation and federal proposals on digital replicas, along with union and guild demands for consent, compensation, and disclosure. Provenance standards and content credentials are likely to become standard attachments to synthetic media deals. International differences in publicity and data protection law will keep cross-border licensing complex. The site's 6,947 state AI bills and 218 compliance and regulation pages suggest that the legal map will keep changing faster than any single contract template.
